target_customer: Skilled nursing facilities, paid directly and through insurers sharing savings from avoided hospital transfers
problem: Nursing home residents in emergencies waited a long time for a physician and were often sent to hospitals. Call9 put a trained specialist on site linked by video to remote emergency physicians.
business_model: Subscription fees from nursing homes plus shared savings with insurers

founders.name: Timothy Peck
founders.background_notes: Physician and co-founder per press coverage.

founders.name: Celina Tenev
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no further background.

exit.reason: Reportedly unable to secure additional funding; about 100 employees laid off, per Becker's

technical_complexity.rationale: Video link plus EKG and telemetry streaming is standard engineering, but running on site clinical staff and 24 hour physician coverage was operationally hard.

defensibility.rationale: Contracts with nursing homes created some lock in, but telehealth vendors and physician groups could offer similar services.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying it. It ran out of funding in 2019.

market_need_then: Hospital transfers from nursing homes are costly. Call9's founder claimed it cut transfers by more than 50 percent, a company claim, and insurers were willing to share savings.

branding.domain_note: Used callnine.com, not call9.com; the site returned 503 when checked.

identity.voice_and_tone: Emergency and urgency framing; one profile calls it reinventing the 911 call for nursing homes

brand_strength.rationale: The name nods to 911 (an inference, not sourced) but the digit and spelled domain differ, and no brand press beyond business coverage was found.

outcome_analysis: Call9 raised about 34 million dollars across a Series A in 2016 and a Series B in 2017 and scaled to roughly 100 employees. It shut down in mid 2019 after reportedly failing to raise more money. Its model needed paid on site staff and insurer shared savings, which suggests the unit economics did not support further growth, though the company did not publish a full post mortem.
notes: The unit_economics factor is an inference from the business model and reported funding failure, not a stated cause. Failory style sites claim other details (200 employees peak, Medicare coding) that were not verified. A search snippet puts the company in YC Spring 2015 while the directory says Summer 2015. No dated competitor sources found, so the list is empty. Founder Peck started Curve Health afterward.
